Foreshadowing can make or break a story. Almost every single story we see in modern games/movies/TV makes use of foreshadowing, and sometimes it's done brilliantly. Walken's character shouldn't have been begging, but maybe made a joke or said something about being rescued if something happened in passing, that would've worked better?

Is foreshadowing at its best when you can't guess what it's foreshadowing? You know it's something but that's it, and then when it happens you feel smart for seeing the foreshadow?

Foreshadowing is really hard to avoid. Without foreshadowing you are left with a nihilistic story where everything happens without any reason and it's boring to watch (for example, Gummo). Even stories without a plot will have foreshadowing (for example, Clerks) and if done right you don't even notice it unless you watch it over again.

In the case of The Deer Hunters, there are two ways I would have written it if I could...

1) Instead of Walken begging to be saved, have DeNero begging to be saved. Because then when Walken goes AWOL it would have been a twist in the plot and DeNero would have come to the realization that he needed to do what he begged Walken to do. It would have made for a much better character development. Or...

2) Not even have the begging. When Walken ran out of the wedding drunk and naked, keep all the dialogue but take out all that "if shit hits the fan, save me" part.
